subject: SLA exception request: canary/A-B rollout as SLA mitigation
messages:
From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: acme.ops@acme.com
Date: Sun, 02 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA exception request: production rollout instability

Monica,

Thanks again for the call earlier. We're seeing intermittent latency spikes and a couple of 503s during our weekend release window when traffic tipples during regional failover. Our procurement team has asked for an official SLA exception and a mitigation plan while we run a longer validation of your new serving runtime on our workload.

High level:
- Problem window: daily 02:00–04:00 PST for the past 3 weekends
- Impact: transient latency up to 1.8s P95, occasional 5xx responses (~0.02% requests)
- Business ask: temporary SLA exception for month of Nov while we complete canary validation; prefer a technical mitigation clause (canary/A-B rollout + automatic fallback + version pinning) rather than credits.

Can you outline how Redwood would formalize canary/A-B rollouts as an acceptable mitigation in the exception (i.e., automatic fallback thresholds, pinning to specific model/build, and controls we can audit)? We also need a contact for operational escalations during the window.

Attaching the metrics snapshot and a blank exception form we can sign.

Thanks,
John
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Cloud

Attachment: runtime-metrics.csv (CSV, 85KB)
Attachment: sla-exception-form.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA exception request: production rollout instability

John — thanks for the clear summary and the metrics. We're sorry for the instability during your release window; we want to make this as low-friction as possible.

Short answer: yes, Redwood can accept a temporary exception documented in your SLA addendum that specifies canary/A-B rollout-based mitigation. Below is a proposed operational definition we use internally — happy to adapt to your legal/ops constraints.

Proposed mitigation clause (summary):
- Canary/A-B rollout: Redwood will perform progressive rollouts (canary then A/B), with traffic ramping at pre-agreed step intervals (e.g., 1%, 5%, 25%, 100%).
- Automatic fallback: If P95 latency or error rate exceed thresholds at any step, traffic is automatically rolled back to the previous stable variant. Thresholds can be defined per route (suggested defaults: P95 > 800ms OR 5xx rate > 0.1%).
- Version pinning: Customer may pin to a model version or runtime build; Redwood will honor pinned versions and will not auto-upgrade pinned endpoints without customer consent.
- Auditability: All rollouts/fallbacks are logged with timestamps, orchestration logs, and KV cache state snapshots; Redwood will provide read-only links to those logs for the duration of the exception (retention: 90 days).

Operational contact for the window: Rishi (on-call, infra) and Grace (CS lead) — cc'd. Stephanie will coordinate the contract addendum.

Next steps: 1) confirm thresholds you want in the addendum, 2) sign the exception form, 3) we run a supervised canary on Wednesday 11/05.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
Mobile: +1 415-555-0192

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 04 Nov 2025 10:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA exception request: production rollout instability

John, Monica — adding technical detail so the addendum is actionable.

Canary/A-B rollout implementation (details):
- Ramp plan: 1% -> 5% (30m) -> 25% (1h) -> 100% (2h). Each step requires both health and SLO checks to pass.
- Health checks: per-step checks include:
  - P95 latency measured over a moving 5m window
  - 5xx and 4xx error rates over same window
  - Resource saturation signals (GPU memory pressure, CPU steal)
- Automatic fallback policy:
  - If any one check breaches threshold for two consecutive windows, orchestrator triggers automatic rollback to previous variant and opens a coordinator ticket.
  - Rollback preserves KV cache state where possible and issues a cache rehydrate event to avoid cold-start latency spikes.
- Version pinning semantics:
  - Pin is at the endpoint level and is sticky until customer unpins or requests upgrade via canary. Pinned endpoints will continue to run the pinned quantized model and kernel set.
- Telemetry and proofs:
  - We will provide a tamper-evident rollout log (immutable audit entries) and an S3 export of step-level metrics.

Operational note: If Acme prefers credits instead of an exception, we can propose a hybrid (partial credit + extended support) but your preference for a technical mitigation is fine.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 06 Nov 2025 14:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA exception request: production rollout instability

All — quick legal/contract note for the addendum draft: please include the following as explicit items.
- Scope & duration: exception effective 2025-11-05 through 2025-12-05; auto-terminates unless renewed.
- Acceptance criteria: definition of "successful canary" (no threshold breach for 24h after reaching 100% or a signed acceptance from Acme ops).
- Escalation path: Redwood will assign a named escalation lead (Rishi) and an on-call pager; severity 1 pages during the rollout window.
- Audit & data access: read-only links to rollout logs and a CSV export (we provided sample). Any additional forensic requests to be handled via Redwood's standard support SLA.

Please review and approve; I can turn this into an addendum and send for signature (DocuSign link included in related_links).

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, acme.ops@acme.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 07 Nov 2025 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA exception request: production rollout instability

John — we appreciate the quick turnaround. Summary and agreed actions: 
1) Redwood will provide a one-month SLA exception (2025-11-05 to 2025-12-05) with canary/A-B rollout mitigation and automatic fallback as described.
2) Thresholds proposed: P95 > 800ms OR 5xx rate > 0.1% at any step triggers automatic rollback. Please confirm if you want tighter thresholds.
3) Acme may pin any endpoint to a model/runtime version; Redwood will not auto-upgrade pinned endpoints.
4) Audit artifacts: rollout logs + CSV export available; support ticket created INF-4321.
5) DocuSign addendum link sent — please sign to formalize.

Planned supervised canary: 2025-11-05 01:30 PST. Rishi will be on-call; Grace will monitor customer metrics.

If this matches your expectation, sign the attached exception form and we'll execute the canary as planned.

Best,
Monica
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
